Pairwise comparisons were conducted between predefined experimental conditions within each colonocyte cluster. Comparisons were performed only when at least 20 cells were available in at least one condition. When one of the conditions contained fewer than 20 cells, we supplemented with cells from other clusters of the same condition that were defined as nearest neighbours of the other condition, using get.knnx of the FNN package with k = 1 based on Euclidean distance in the top 20 principal component space. Differential expression testing was performed using the wilcoxauc function of the presto R package on normalized RNA expression values. We identified DEGs between conditions per cluster using the wilcoxauc function by the presto package, with cut-offs adjusted P < 0.05, pct_in > 10 and logFC > 0.1.

We then pooled genes defined as significant DEGs in at least one comparison in at least one cluster as the union set of condition DEGs. We then calculated the colonocyte average expression levels of each condition. We calculated the expression difference between WTOut and non-infected—namely, diff_WT_vs_NI, where positive values indicate upregulation in WTOut versus non-infected—and between WTIn and WTOut—namely, diff_WT_GFP_vs_WT, where positive values indicate upregulation in WTIn versus WTOut. We ranked the gene according to diff_WT_vs_NI, took the top 50 genes as feature genes and used the AddModuleScore function to calculate the luminal effect gene module score, and applied the same procedure for diff_WT_GFP_vs_WT values for intracellular effect gene module score.

Sources indicate that we used CellChat (v2)84 to infer intracellular communications between co-cultured intestinal epithelial cells and TRM cells. Normalized expression data were extracted from the epithelium and TRM cell combined Seurat RNA assay, and cell-type labels were used to group cells for interaction analysis. We used the built-in human CellChatDB database as reference for ligand–receptor interactions. To reduce computational cost, we subsetted the expression data to include only signalling genes present in the database. Overexpressed genes and interactions were identified using the identifyOverExpressedGenes and identifyOverExpressedInteractions functions. Communication probabilities were computed using the computeCommunProb function with type = truncatedMean and trim = 0.05. We subsetted to interactions between proximal small intestinal enterocytes and immune cell types, excluding proliferating CD4+ T cells for visualization.

Read alignment, gene expression quantification and cell filtering of the VASA-seq data were performed by Single Cell Discoveries. In brief, raw sequencing data were processed using Cutadapt (v4.9) to remove adapter sequences and homopolymers, followed by Ribodetector (v0.3.1) to filter out ribosomal reads. Processed reads were then aligned to the reference genome using STARsolo (v2.7.11b), with the parameter–soloFeatures set to GeneFull_Ex50pAS. The human reference genome used was GRCh38, ENSEMBL release 103. The S.Tm reference genome was downloaded from EnsemblBacteria Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium str. 14028S str. LT2 14028S (GCA_000022165) release 62. The resulting single-cell-level gene count matrices were used as inputs for downstream analysis in R.

It has been revealed that to improve the gene annotation for the S.Tm genome, we performed sequence alignment for the genes in the S.Tm strain 14028S annotation against the S.Tm strain 14028 annotation (GCF_028596185.1_ASM2859618v1). Out of the 1,542 genes with Ensembl-style identifiers beginning with ENSB, 242 were mapped to annotated genes with common names in the S.Tm 14028 annotation by blastn85,86 with more than 90% of sequence similarity.

According to recent reports, cells without GFP signal, UMI count of less than 3,500 or External RNA Controls Consortium (ERCC) counts of less than 450 were excluded. Raw counts were normalized using the NormalizeData function in Seurat with a scale factor of 10,000.

According to FACS index sorting values, cells with GFP < 500 were defined as GFP−, 500 or more and less than 2,000 as GFPlo, 2,000 or more and 10,000 or less as GFPint, and more than 10,000 as GFPhi. For human genes, only genes detected in at least 10% of cells in at least one GFP signal group were included in the differentially expressed test. For each retained gene, expression was modelled using two nested linear models. The reduced model included log-transformed total UMI counts per cell and the percentage of mitochondrial reads as technical covariates, whereas the full model additionally included the GFP signal group as a factor. The contribution of the GFP signal group was assessed by ANOVA comparing the full and reduced models. Genes with Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted P < 0.05 were considered differentially expressed. To assign directionality, we calculated the difference in average expression between the GFPhi and GFPlo groups and assigned the directionality accordingly.

For S.Tm, we applied the same differentially expressed test strategy, but only included GFP+ cells for comparison. Given the sparsity of the bacteria transcripts, we reduced the detection rate cut-off to 1%. After further excluding ERCC transcripts and features with Ensembl-style identifiers beginning with ENSB, 3,137 genes were left as input for the differentially expressed test. We used nominal P < 0.05 as the cut-off to get marginally significant bacterial DEG.

The raw and processed sorted infection scRNA-seq and VASA-seq data could be accessed via E-MTAB-17487 and E-MTAB-17486. Additional supporting materials, including processed single-cell data with cell-type annotation, statistically significant differentially accessible chromatin regions upon S.Tm infection and transcription factor–target regulomes inferred by Pando based on the S.Tm infection dataset are available at Mendeley Data (https://doi.org/10.17632/3jpvw4t4gr). Fragment files of scMultiome are available at Mendeley Data (https://doi.org/10.17632/8pt6w6fc7m). The raw mass spectrometry proteomic files and corresponding metadata tables and scripts used are available in the MassIVE repository (UCSD) under the accession code MSV000102372. The raw flow cytometry data files used to generate the immune UMAP have been deposited in the Zenodo repository87 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21786694). Source data underlying all graphical representations used in the figures are provided as Supplementary Information. Public adult intestine multi-region scRNA-seq datasets were retrieved from an interactive website of the Space-Time Gut Cell Atlas (https://www.gutcellatlas.org/)79, ArrayExpress (E-MTAB-10187)81 and Gene Expression Omnibus (GSE185224)80.

The core scripts of single-cell data analysis are available on GitHub (https://github.com/devsystemslab/Host-microbe_interaction_model/).

R.L.-S., M.F.H., Q.Y., M.N., N.G. and J.G.C. conceived the study. R.L.-S., M.F.H., Q.Y., N.G. and J.G.C. wrote the manuscript. M.N. designed and fabricated the fluidic device and crypt stamps, with support from J.A. and S.M. M.P.L. contributed to the development of the fluidic device holding the tissues. M.N. and R.L.-S. generated the artwork design. M.F.H. and R.L.-S. designed and performed most of the experiments in the article. R.L.-S., M.F.H., M.N., N.A. and J.B. optimized the epithelium growth conditions. M.F.H. isolated the organoid lines and TRM cells from primary tissue. R.L.-S., M.F.H., M.A.-B., L.G.-T. and S.S. performed scRNA-seq, scMultiome and VASA-seq experiments. M.A.-B. and L.G.-T. generated the sequencing libraries. Q.Y. performed the computational analysis of scRNA-seq and scMultiome data, with support and data interpretation from R.L.-S., S.S. and M.F.H. M.F.H., R.L.-S. and J.A. co-developed the histomold. I.C. and S.T. performed the FFPE processing, sectioning, H&E and AlcianBlue–PAS stainings, with support from M.F.H. M.F.H. performed the immunohistochemistry and mIF stainings, imaging and analysis with support from R.L.-S. and M.N. M.F.H., R.L.-S., M.N. and L.K. performed whole-mount stainings and imaging. M.F.H., K.K. and S.K. performed the flow cytometry experiments and analysis of immune cells. R.L.-S., D.C. and I.C.-A. performed the flow cytometry and image stream experiments and analysis of epithelial cells. L.K., A.M.F. and M.F.H. performed the cytokine measurements. N.A., S.R.V., Y.B. and J.B. generated the organoid reporter lines. J.F., A.A. and C.S. performed and processed the proteomic measurements. Live imaging was performed by M.F.H., R.L.-S. and M.N., and analysed by M.B. M.H. and D.B. generated and provided the S.Tm strains. T.R. and F.G. supported with data interpretation. All authors read and approved the manuscript.

All authors, with the exception of M.H., F.G. and D.B., are current employees of Hoffmann-La Roche or were employed by the company while working on this study. The company provided support in the form of salaries for authors but did not have any additional role in the study design, data collection and analysis, decision to publish or preparation of the manuscript. All authors declare no additional competing interests. Hoffmann-La Roche has filed for patent protection on the organ-on-chip and histomold technology described here. M.N., M.P.L. and N.G. are named as inventors on the organ-on-chip patent, with the application number WO 2025/202125 A1. M.F.H., R.L.-S. and J.A. are named as inventors on the histomold patent, with the application number WO 2026/037916 A1.

a) Picture of a chip-slide with culture medium, including a 3D-rendered image of the cross-section of the chip-slide containing three individual chip segments and an image of the micropatterned stamp with a representative bright-field image of an engineered intestine cross-section, e > 15. b) Time course of biomimetic epithelium formation from the stamped empty ECM to epithelium coverage and maturation. Scale bars: 500 µm. c) Quantification of viable crypts of 16 donors from duodenum, ileum and colon, d = 16. d) Representative EDF brightfield image of a Z-stack, showing the top-view of a day-9 epithelium, e = 3. Scale bar: 200 µm. The magnified insert (top) shows a 3D-reconstruction of the epithelium with crypts penetrating into the matrix. The magnified insert (bottom) shows an EDF image of a Z-stack in the crypt area. Scale bar: 50 µm. e) Representative EDF fluorescent image of selected Z-stacks with magnified insert, showing an iCas9 CDH1-mScarlet3 day-9 duodenal epithelium with tight E-Cadherin+ adherens junctions (red), e = 6. Scale bar: 100 µm. f) Overview of the high-throughput histo-processing workflow using 3D-printed histomold facilitating co-planar embedding of up to fifty engineered epithelia at once. Post-FFPE embedding, dozens of engineered epithelia can be visualized within one section as illustrated in a representative H&E. Consecutive sections subjected to H&E and mIF to evaluate the spatial organization and maturation of a duodenal epithelium at day 6. Scale bar: 100 µm. g) H&E cross-sections of representative colon engineered epithelium and primary tissue, showing high morphological similarity, crypt depth, and goblet cell distribution, e = 5. Scale bars: 100 µm.

a-c) Representative mIF cross-section of engineered duodenal, ileal and colonic epithelia in direct comparison to the donor-matched primary tissue (ileum not matched), highlighting the stem-niche specific SOX9+ (cyan) and transit-amplifying Ki67+ cells (pink), matching abundance of MUC2+ goblet cells (green) and high expression of the region-enriched absorptive lineage marker (orange) in the E-Cadherin+ epithelium (grey). The duodenal epithelium was marked by strong expression APOA4+ enterocytes, matching the parental tissue. Expression of distal FABP6+ enterocytes in the top-layer of the engineered epithelium matched ileal tissue. The colonic epithelium exhibited CA1+ colonocytes at comparable levels to the organ of origin, e = 4. Scale bars: 50 µm.

#106337. Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat

📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (917 w)

Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (917 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat stated.
  • Themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a significant win.
  • "It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat stated. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a big relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome.".

Themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a significant win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

"I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat noted. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed.".

Growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," noted Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

Recent findings suggest that "I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat said. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

Sources indicate that "I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat mentioned. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a substantial change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships.".

As well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat said, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat said.

It has been revealed that "So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she mentioned. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself.".

That has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

According to recent reports, "The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

It has been revealed that should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she mentioned.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride.".

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.
  • Hansi Flick has been left with a defensive headache ahead of this weekend's clash with Villarreal, with both Andreas Christensen and Pau Cubarsi suffering from injuries.
  • Flick confirmed Christensen would miss the next two matches after sustaining a calf problem in training, having only just returned from an injury lay-off earlier in the month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Hansi Flick has been left with a defensive headache ahead of this weekend's clash with Villarreal, with both Andreas Christensen and Pau Cubarsi suffering from injuries.

Flick confirmed Christensen would miss the next two matches after sustaining a calf problem in training, having only just returned from an injury lay-off earlier in the month.

The Danish defender played 30 minutes of Barcelona's 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid before the international break, but his absence offers Flick a problem he must try and tackle.

Cubarsi is another player likely to miss out on Sunday's clash after he was injured during Spain's 3-2 defeat to England in the Nations League, with the 19-year-old replaced at half-time having given away a penalty on Harry Kane in the first half.

"Andreas was really in a good moment, so this is why the decision was made not to go with the national team so he could train here," Flick remarked of Christensen's injury.

"I think it was the right decision, but unfortunately he's out for maybe two games. He is really disappointed.

"For me, when fit, he's one of the best central defenders. We give him our support and also we have to help him to maybe improve a little physically.".

When asked about Cubarsi's glitch, Flick added: "It's not a big thing, but we have to take care. He could be on the bench [vs. Villarreal] and we will see if he travels to Baku.

"With Cuba, he played amazingly last season, but with the World Cup he had a lot of minutes, and he's only 19 years old. So, it's now about taking care of him.".

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 21, 2026.

It remains to be seen who Flick will deploy in his reshuffled back line, with Xavi Espart, who signed a upcoming long-term contract earlier this week, also out with an injury.

Joules Kounde and Eric Garcia are, however, available again after recovering from knocks, though Flick does have a more unconventional solution in Frenkie de Jong.

De Jong impressed at right-back during Barcelona's win over Atletico, and the Blaugrana boss hinted the Netherlands international could be utilised there again.

Recent findings suggest that "We will see," Flick added. "I am very happy with Frenkie. He felt something [with the national team] but it was a small injury and he is available.".

Higher up the pitch, Dani Olmo is set for his first appearance since October after recovering from an injury, but Rodri remains out with a hamstring problem.

Sources indicate that "We have to wait day by day, but I think it's a good moment," Flick remarked of Rodri's fitness. "We also take care about this because, last season with Manchester City, he had a similar injury.

"I spoke this morning with him, and it took a little bit longer than they expected, so now we have to take care. It's not the same injury, it's not the big injury like he had in the past, but I think we have to take care.".

Fermin has been involved in 12 goals in 11 games in the 2026-27 LaLiga season (seven goals and five assists).

No midfielder has generated more after their first 11 games of a season in the competition in the 21st century (also 12 for Angel Di Maria in 2011-12, Cesc Fabregas in 2011-12 and Jude Bellingham in 2023-24).

Moreno has been involved in five goals in 14 LaLiga appearances against Barcelona (three goals, two assists), scoring or assisting in his last two.

MATCH PREDICTION: BARCELONA WIN.

Despite being favoured in the pre-match simulations, Barcelona have lost two of their last five LaLiga matches against Villarreal (W3), twice as many defeats as they suffered in their previous 29 meetings with them in the competition (W22 D6 L1).

Indeed, after a run of 10 consecutive home wins against Villarreal in LaLiga between 2010 and 2020, Barcelona have lost three of their last five home games against them in the competition (W2).

Since the 2021-22 season, Barcelona have not suffered more home defeats in LaLiga against any other opponent than they have against Villarreal (P5 W2 D0 L3), also three against Real Madrid (P6 W3 D0 L3).

Barcelona have, however, earned 33 points from 12 games in the 2026-27 LaLiga season (W11 L1). Counting three points for a win, they have only accumulated more points at this stage of the competition in the 2012-13, 2013-14 and 2017-18 seasons (34 points – W11 D1), also earning 33 points in the 2024-25 season (W11 L1).

Flick's side have also outperformed their expected goals by more than any other LaLiga side this season (+8.4, with 48 goals from 39.6 xG), while Villarreal have underperformed theirs by the most (-7.4, with 17 goals from 24.4 xG).

And they face a Villarreal side that have picked up seven points from their last four LaLiga games (W2 D1 L1), just one point fewer than they managed in their first eight games (eight points – P8 W2 D2 L4).

Konyaspor will be looking to halt their recent slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Besiktas to Medas Konya Buyuksehir Stadyumu on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with eight points from 11 matches, only outside the bottom three on goal difference, while the Black Eagles occupy fifth place with 19 points from 10 games and will be hoping to maintain their push towards the top of the standings.

Konyaspor have endured a difficult run of results in recent weeks, winning just once in their last six league matches and struggling to find consistency in the final third.

Ilhan Palut's side began that sequence with consecutive goalless draws against Kasimpasa and Istanbul Basaksehir before suffering a 1-0 defeat away to Amed SK.

They then recorded a 2-0 home victory over Genclerbirligi, but that proved to be their only success during the period as they suffered consecutive defeats against Galatasaray (4-0) and Samsunspor (1-0).

Konyaspor were particularly disappointing in their defeat away to Samsunspor just before the break, failing to take anything from a match against a side sitting second-bottom and enduring a losing run.

The result further highlighted their struggles in front of goal, with the hosts having scored just six times in their opening 11 league matches, an average of fewer than one per game, while they have failed to find the net in seven of those fixtures.

Konyaspor have scored four of their six goals and collected seven of their eight points on home soil, although they were thrashed by Galatasaray in their last home game and now face a Besiktas side that have beaten them in their last two league meetings.

The hosts did manage to defeat the Black Eagles 1-0 in their most recent encounter, although that victory came in the Turkish Cup.

Besiktas, meanwhile, have enjoyed a more productive campaign, collecting seven wins, one draw and three defeats from their opening 11 league matches to remain within reach of the leading teams, sitting six points behind league leaders Galatasaray.

Vincenzo Italiano's side are also unbeaten in their last three league games, a sequence that began with a 2-0 home victory over Istanbul Basaksehir before they were held to a 2-2 draw by Kasimpasa.

Their subsequent European fixture saw them suffer a 3-2 defeat against Celtic, but they responded positively three days later by recording a convincing 3-0 home win over Genclerbirligi.

Dusan Vlahovic was particularly influential in that victory, scoring twice as the Black Eagles returned to winning ways in the Super Lig and demonstrated the attacking quality that has made them one of the more productive sides in the division, with only four teams scoring more than their 23 goals.

However, the visitors have struggled on the road, winning just one of their five away league matches and failing to win any of their last three, during which they have recorded one draw and two defeats.

Roberto De Zerbi has issued a worrying update on Savio after the Tottenham forward was forced off shorting after returning from injury.

The Brazilian was making his first appearance in over a month, since suffering a muscular problem against Manchester United in October.

Savio came off the bench to replace the dazzling debutant Luca Williams-Barnett, who scored one and assisted another on his first senior start for Spurs.

As the game approached the 90th minute, Savio pulled up after being dispossessed and immediately pulled his shirt over his head.

After being attended to by the club’s medical team, Savio was replaced by Archie Gray to see out the 2-0 win over Ipswich.

Speaking at full-time, De Zerbi admitted he had reaggravated the same injury which had kept him sidelined for the last few weeks.

"Yes, I'm very angry about that, because Savio is a crucial player for us,” mentioned the Italian.

“What he can make and he has to make the difference for us. It is the same injury. And it is the worst thing from today.”.

It is not absolutely clear how long Savio will now be sidelined, with Tottenham next in action away at Sunderland next Sunday.

Savio’s injury comes after Sandro Tonali missed out on a place in the matchday squad due to illness.

Trabzonspor will look to extend their winning run in the league to seven games when they host bottom-placed Eyupspor at Papara Park on Sunday.

The Black Sea outfit sit second in the Turkish Super Lig standings with 25 points from 11 matches, three behind league leaders Galatasaray, while the visitors are 18th with just three points, five adrift of safety.

Thomas Reis has made an excellent start to his reign, winning all six of his league games in charge, with the latest victory coming in a 2-0 away triumph over Alanyaspor just before the international break, as Wagner Pina opened the scoring in the 17th minute before Muhammed Salah doubled their advantage in the 34th.

That result represented a strong response to their 1-0 defeat to Freiburg in the Conference League, which brought an end to their seven-game winning streak across all competitions.

Trabzonspor will now look to begin another run of victories, and their attacking and defensive records suggest they have every reason to be confident, having scored 26 goals, the fourth-highest tally in the division, while conceding just eight, the fewest in the league, as they build a strong foundation in their pursuit of a first league title since 2021-22.

The hosts have also won all five of their league games at home this season, and another victory would see them match the club's best start to a home league campaign, last achieved in 1984-85.

Meanwhile, Eyupspor are in deep trouble after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Kocaelispor last time out, their eighth consecutive league loss and the ninth time in 11 matches this season that they have failed to score in the division.

No other side has conceded more goals than Eyupspor this season, with their tally standing at 30, while they have also scored just three times, the fewest in the league.

Mustafa Dalci said after the defeat to Kocaelispor that his side are entering a period in which they must start collecting points, but their prospects look bleak ahead of another difficult away fixture, particularly as they have conceded a league-high 19 goals on their travels.

Their head-to-head record against Trabzonspor offers little encouragement either, with Eyupspor yet to win any of their four previous meetings, drawing one and losing three, while they have failed to score in all four encounters.

The hosts sit 12th in the Turkish Super Lig standings after 11 matches, while the visitors occupy 10th place and will be hoping to bounce back from their latest defeat to maintain their push towards the upper half of the table.

Erzurumspor had enjoyed an encouraging spell before their recent setbacks, recording victories over Eyupspor and Gaziantep, as well as a draw with Alanyaspor and a win against Samsunspor, to put together a four-game unbeaten run and move away from the lower reaches of the standings.

However, their momentum was checked when they suffered a 3-1 home defeat against Corum before losing 2-1 away to Caykur Rizespor in their most recent league outing before the international break.

Erzurumspor took the lead against Rizespor through Ibrahim Diabate, but they were unable to hold on to their advantage as the hosts turned the contest around, leaving Serkan Ozbalta's side with consecutive defeats after they had collected 10 points from their preceding four matches.

Despite those setbacks, the hosts will be encouraged by their home performances this season, having beaten Konyaspor, Eyupspor and Samsunspor while suffering defeats against Galatasaray and Corum, the latter being their most recent appearance in front of their supporters.

They will be keen to rediscover the defensive organisation that helped them secure those three victories without conceding, particularly against a Goztepe side that has demonstrated considerable attacking quality in recent weeks.

This will be the fifth Super Lig meeting between the sides, with Erzurumspor picking up two wins, drawing one and losing one of the previous four, although they have lost their last two encounters against the visitors, one in the Turkish Cup and the other in the second division.

Goztepe, meanwhile, had been enjoying an impressive run of results before their latest setback, winning four consecutive league matches as part of a six-game unbeaten streak to establish themselves in the top half of the table.

Stanimir Stoilov's side began that sequence with a 4-0 away victory over Eyupspor before recording a 2-1 win against Kocaelispor and a 2-0 home triumph over Corum.

The visitors then produced one of their most impressive performances of the campaign by defeating Fenerbahce 2-1 away from home.

However, their winning streak came to an end just before the break when they suffered a 2-1 home defeat against Istanbul Basaksehir, with Juan finding the net but the hosts ultimately unable to prevent their opponents from taking all three points.

Goztepe nevertheless have an away unbeaten run to protect, with Goz Goz having gone four games without defeat on the road, winning their last three and drawing the other.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Roberto De Zerbi believes Luca Williams-Barnett's "talent is bigger than this performance" after the 18-year-old impressed on his first start for Tottenham against Ipswich Town.

Williams-Barnett tucked away Pedro Porro's cross in the 15th minute to net his first goal for Spurs, sending the home fans into raptures in north London.

Further chances fell to Mohammed Kudus and Jan Paul van Hecke, before Dominic Solanke struck in the 51st minute to cap off a move that once again involved Williams-Barnett, sealing a 2-0 victory for Spurs.

At 18 years and 51 days old, Williams-Barnett became the youngest player to score for Tottenham in the Premier League since Gareth Bale struck against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).

And his performance has certainly left a big impression on De Zerbi, who had previously labelled the starlet "one of the best young players I have ever worked with.".

"He's played very well, but his talent is bigger than this performance," De Zerbi told BBC Match of the Day.

"It was the first game, and I am very happy. I am very delighted with his performance, but he is a major, big, big talent.

"The management of the younger talented players is different because you can't take risks to lose their enthusiasm and their positive mentality.

"But I think Tottenham's dressing room now is a good environment for him.

"I put James [Maddison] to play very close to him to speak the same language but also to help him and put him in the best conditions to play. To play with freedom, to play with his qualities because his qualities are very massive.

"He's a mature guy. He is smart and understands the situation. He has great behaviour inside the group and the group is good enough to help him stay calm and to play without pressure, because he has to enjoy it on the pitch.

"He has to work hard but also he has to keep the passion to keep the love of football.".

“I am happy because he played with enjoyment, with passion, without pressure.”  Roberto De Zerbi was full of praise for Luca Williams-Barnett after today's win!

— Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) November 21, 2026.

Williams-Barnett (18y 51d) became the sixth-youngest player to start a Premier League game for Tottenham, after Stephen Carr (17y 28d), Mikey Moore (17y 77d), Andy Turner (17y 145d), Philip Ifil (17y 270d) and Gareth Bale (18y 41d).

The youngster also became the fourth-youngest player to score on his first Premier League start, behind Daniel Jebbison in May 2021 (17y 276d), Danny Cadamarteri in September 1997 (17y 343d), and Mark Cullen in May 2010 (18y 12d).

Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil, meanwhile, admitted that his side were not at their best at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Indeed, Ipswich are now winless across their last five top-flight games, and they have conceded in each of their last 30 Premier League matches.

"We gave them a really soft first goal, which obviously gives them some comfort," O'Neil stated.

"And then we didn't get to our level enough today. We got into some good attacking situations, but we didn't show enough quality.

"We should have dealt with both goals better. So all in all, we can't argue with the result. They were better than us which we have to accept.".

#106327. What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one issue ranked above all others: the economy.
  • So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?
  • Sources indicate that markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one issue ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

Sources indicate that markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

With Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already mentioned he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, noted in a note.

"I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

Industry observers note that some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

Kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, said the vote highlighted the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of substantial tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

According to recent reports, "This election shows that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he stated. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

If the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown remarked, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

That sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

In a recent development, "Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

Industry observers note that trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard mentioned, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump stated in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election problem — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

According to recent reports, "You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard said. "From a political point of view, that's the most important thing now.".

It has been revealed that george Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he remarked in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and issues.

Industry observers note that yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another issue vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the fresh Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic issues to secure his political survival.

Industry observers note that "Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard remarked. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted he was not involved in any wrongdoing at his former club Manchester City – but refused to rule out taking action against them if their appeal fails.

In a recent development, in his first sit-down interview in five months, broadcast on Friday, Berrada tackled a range of topics concerning United but his links to City, from whom he joined United in 2024, were also brought up. He worked at the club during some of the period that City were found to have broken Premier League rules.

Back in September, an independent regulatory commission found City guilty of a multitude of charges brought against them by the Premier League, with financial offences ranging between 2009 and 2018.

The scathing verdict determined that City had 'artificially inflated' their revenues and reduced costs through 'disguised funding' schemes such as 'sham' contracts.

Berrada joined City in 2011 before going on to become their chief operating officer in 2016, raising questions over whether he could end up implicated if City – who vehemently contest the charges – fail in their appeal.

'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted. 'I want to be very clear about this, right. I wasn't involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn't involved in the proceedings; there are no allegations against me, and in that sense there will be no surprises.'.

Asked if United would push for compensation should City's guilty verdict be upheld on appeal, Berrada remained tight-lipped.

Omar Berrada joined Manchester City in 2011... and moved across the city 13 years later.

Berrada has become one of the main sources of anger among United fans who have campaigned against the owners and the board.

Industry observers note that 'I don't want to comment on that because right now it's an ongoing process,' he added. 'When it runs its course we'll take our view of where is our position as Manchester United.'.

Berrada was not used as a witness in the original investigation and there are no allegations directed specifically to the now-United CEO.

City boss Enzo Maresca, meanwhile, insisted that the guilty verdicts handed down to Manchester City for financial chicanery have not affected his players despite three consecutive Premier League defeats.

City fell six points behind defending champions Arsenal in the weeks before this month’s international break amid a slew of individual high-profile errors that led to claims of Maresca’s squad being preoccupied by the uncertainty surrounding the club.

The Premier League have a range of available sanctions to them were City to lose an appeal set for next month. Those would likely result in relegation to the Championship.

But Maresca does not equate that looming doomsday backdrop with a worrying run of form before they face Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday lunchtime.

Industry observers note that ‘I don't think the players are thinking too much about that,’ Maresca remarked. ‘If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, look at [Aston] Villa away. We had so many chances, for instance Iliman [Ndiaye] hit the post, or Brighton where the keeper was man of the match.

Enzo Maresca insists his stars are not thinking about the impact of the guilty verdict.

Erling Haaland states he is 'incredibly' happy to be a City player and tops the Premier League scoring charts with nine so far this campaign.

According to recent reports, ‘Then [Nottingham] Forest when Erling [Haaland] had the chance to score for 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise. I don't think they are worried about that.’.

Haaland claimed to be ‘incredibly happy’ about being a City player in a defiant interview with Norwegian television earlier in the week, although few others have addressed the problems publicly.

Marc Guehi has previously stated the players are ‘relaxed’, while Phil Foden refused to discuss it when asked.

Maresca has spent the past fortnight analysing City’s ten league matches and has admitted that the team requires more balance after conceding too many goals to turnovers or counter attacks.

‘I was not thinking that we were doing everything well when we were winning games and I'm not thinking that we did everything wrong when we lost games,’ the Italian added.

In a recent development, ‘For me it is the beginning of something long. I think we are attacking well because we are creating chances and overall we are controlling games.

Sources indicate that ‘There are moments we are not controlling and we have to realise the reasons why and do better. We are conceding goals and most are avoidable from my point of view.’.

There have been occasions – like the first goal at Forest – when City’s building from the back has put them in serious trouble. Josko Gvardiol lost the ball at the City Ground after no midfielder had shown for possession.

It has been revealed that maresca noted: ‘We reviewed things during the break. The idea is to continue to attack in the same way and try to find the balance when we defend or when we are building like what happened for the first goal against Forest.

‘When you are building and you lose the ball in the build-up it's difficult to build with that.’.

The Frenchman sustained the injury in a behind-closed-doors game against West Ham United during the international break.

Revealing the extent of the injury, Alvaro Arbeloa told reporters on Friday: "Unfortunately, Lecomte injured his Achilles tendon against West Ham, so he will be out for the rest of the season.

Lecomte has not played in the Premier League this season, but he featured in three of Fulham’s EFL Cup games, including a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace last month.

The news of Smith Rowe's physical concern represents the latest setback in what is proving to be a difficult campaign for the Arsenal academy product.

The 28-year-old made 37 Premier League appearances in Marco Silva's final season in charge, but he has featured in just four league games under Arbeloa due to injury and selection decisions.

In more positive news, Arbeloa explained that Tom Cairney could be in contention to return to the squad after missing the draw against Newcastle United before the international window.

If available, Cairney could have a role to play off the bench as Fulham look to end their woeful run of form against Manchester City.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Barney Corkhill | 20 Nov 2026 23:32.
  • Industry observers note that liverpool have won more major trophies than Manchester United, leading the Liverpool vs.
  • With a margin that small, the answer depends on what you count, because leaving out the one-off 1986 Football League Super Cup puts the clubs level, while leaving out the Community Shield gives the Reds a clear lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Barney Corkhill | 20 Nov 2026 23:32.

Industry observers note that liverpool have won more major trophies than Manchester United, leading the Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies count 69-68 on every senior competitive honour as of November 20, 2026.

With a margin that small, the answer depends on what you count, because leaving out the one-off 1986 Football League Super Cup puts the clubs level, while leaving out the Community Shield gives the Reds a clear lead.

Neither club has lifted a trophy since Liverpool's 2024-25 Premier League title, which nudged the Anfield outfit back ahead of their eternal rivals.

Liverpool and Manchester United share the record for English league titles with 20 each, after the Merseysiders' 2024-25 Premier League win matched the total the Red Devils reached in 2012-13.

United are stronger in the FA Cup, with 13 wins to Liverpool's eight, and in the Community Shield, which they have won or shared 21 times against 16 for the Anfield club.

Liverpool hold the record of 10 League Cups, four more than their rivals, and they are the only one of the pair to have won the Football League Super Cup, which was played only once.

The gap opens up in Europe, where six European Cups, three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups give the Reds 13 continental trophies to United's six.

Liverpool have more trophies than Manchester United on the fullest count, one ahead, and they also lead when Community Shields are left out.

United only draw level if the 1986 Football League Super Cup is removed or shared Community Shields are discounted, and they only go ahead on a count limited to the league, FA Cup and League Cup, which they lead 39-38.

That makes the Reds the more decorated club, since they lead or are level on every method that includes European competition, and the only count that favours the Old Trafford side ignores continental silverware altogether.

United's honours board leaves out the Super Cup and so reveals the rivals level, which is a fair reading, but even on that basis the Red Devils still need one more trophy to go ahead.

Opinion is split on whether the Community Shield should count as a genuine trophy, and the FA itself treats it as a friendly for disciplinary purposes, so bookings in it do not carry over into other domestic games.

The fixture has only been contested between the league champions and the FA Cup winners since 1974, and before that it was an invitational match.

Seven of United's Community Shields and three of Liverpool's came before that change, which strengthens the case for leaving the trophy out.

The Anfield club's own honours page lists 52 major men's honours, a figure that excludes both the Community Shield and the Football League Super Cup, and the Community Shield never appeared on the honours board at their old Melwood training ground either.

Counting the Football League Super Cup but not the Community Shield gives the Reds a 53-47 lead, a six-trophy cushion over the Red Devils.

The Football League Super Cup was set up after the Heysel Stadium disaster in May 1985 and the European ban on English clubs that followed, as a replacement competition for the six sides who would have played on the continent in 1985-86.

Liverpool beat Everton in a two-legged final held back until September 1986, winning 3-1 at Anfield and 4-1 at Goodison Park for a 7-2 aggregate victory.

The tournament was never played again, which is why some honours boards ignore it, and counting it or not decides whether the Merseysiders lead or the clubs are level.

A drawn Community Shield used to be shared, and Liverpool's list includes five shared editions (1964, 1965, 1977, 1986 and 1990), while United shared four (1965, 1967, 1977 and 1990).

The years 1965, 1977 and 1990 appear on both lists, and removing every shared Community Shield leaves both clubs on 64, another count where Man United can claim a tie but not a lead.

Manchester United have their strongest case at home, with 60 domestic honours to Liverpool's 55 when Community Shields and the Football League Super Cup are counted.

In the three main domestic competitions, the league, FA Cup and League Cup, the Red Devils lead 39-38 thanks to five more FA Cup wins.

Cup finals between the pair have been split evenly, as United won the 1977 FA Cup final 2-1 and the 1996 final 1-0, while the Reds won the League Cup finals of 1983 and 2003.

The 1983 final went to extra time, with Alan Kennedy and Ronnie Whelan cancelling out Norman Whiteside's opener for a 2-1 win, and Steven Gerrard and Michael Owen scored in the 2-0 win in Cardiff 20 years later.

In a recent development, for every result between the two clubs rather than just the silverware, our Man Utd vs. Liverpool head-to-head record covers each meeting.

Liverpool's six European Cups are more than any other British team has won and double United's three, and that record is what separates the clubs.

The Reds add three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups, while United's six European trophies are completed by a Europa League, a Cup Winners' Cup and one UEFA Super Cup.

United edge the world honours 2-1, having won the 1999 Intercontinental Cup and the 2008 Club World Cup, while the Merseysiders won the Club World Cup in 2019.

For the stories behind several of those European nights, including the 2005 final in Istanbul, our rundown of Liverpool's 10 greatest comebacks goes back through the club's most dramatic recoveries.

Manchester United's modern haul was built under Sir Alex Ferguson, who won 38 trophies in 26 years in charge between 1986 and 2013, including 13 league titles, five FA Cups and two Champions League titles.

The teams behind that run feature heavily in our ranking of Manchester United's 10 greatest ever teams, which sets the Ferguson sides against the club's earlier eras.

The latest swings came in 2023-24, when Liverpool's League Cup win put them one ahead on the full count before the Red Devils beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final to draw level again.

The Reds' 2024-25 Premier League title then put them one clear, while on the count that ignores the Super Cup the same sequence went from a tie to a United lead and back to the current tie.

Liverpool and Manchester United are both in the 2026-27 Champions League league phase, so Europe offers the biggest single swing, alongside the FA Cup, the League Cup and the next Community Shield.

One trophy for United without a reply from Anfield would level the full count, while any Liverpool success would stretch the gap to two.

Liverpool appear to have a better chance of adding to their haul in the 2026-27 campaign, with Man United out of the League Cup and having seen any faint hopes of a title challenge evaporate amidst their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

The Old Trafford side are now led by Mauricio Pochettino, who became head coach in November 2026 after Michael Carrick was sacked.

To see what the upcoming head coach brings, our breakdown of Pochettino's record against every Premier League club shows how his past teams have fared against each top-flight side.

For a view of current strength rather than history, our ranking of the best football teams in the world shows where Liverpool sit among Europe's elite.

Industry observers note that luka Modric may be 41 years of age, but he reveals no signs of slowing down. In fact, he remains crucial or both AC Milan and Croatia.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by pointing out that Sunday’s game will be a first for Modric, even given the hundreds of games he has played. The midfielder will face Frosinone for the first time, the 227th opponent of his long career (155 at club level and 72 for the national team).

In ten days, Modric will have gone from from London’s Wembley Stadium where he faced England, to the Opus Arena in Osijek, Croatia, where he beat the Czech Republic and played 90 minutes as captain, back to San Siro for the Frosinone game.

Industry observers note that yesterday, Luka returned to Milanello and trained with the Rossoneri, ready to take charge of the group again when the tournament resumes. He’s one of the eight players in the squad who have surpassed 800 minutes of total playing time across all competitions, including goalkeepers.

The Ballon d’Or winner has featured 13 times this season, with 11 being in the league (eight starts), and twice as a substitute in the Europa League. For his national team, he’s appeared in six Nations League matches, four of them from the start.

Recent findings suggest that the match against Spain on October 6th was supposed to be his farewell to Croatia, but instead he was easily persuaded to stay and continue. He’s played 19 of the 21 matches since August, accumulating over a thousand minutes – 1,114 to be precise.

Industry observers note that modric scored for Milan at 40 years, five months and four days (the winner against Pisa) and is third in the ranking of the oldest goal scorers in the club’s history. Alessandro Costacurta is second (41 years, 25 days) and Zlatan Ibrahimovic is first (41 years, 5 months, and 15 days).

So, another record is in sight in the present, but what about the future? Modric is tied to Milan until the summer, with his contract expiring in June 2027. There are no further options for an extension but the relationship between player and club goes beyond written agreements.

According to recent reports, luka will decide his own future, as he did last summer, choosing to stay. He still wanted Milan despite being left behind without his family (who had since returned to Madrid) out of love for the Rossoneri. Next season, who knows?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.
  • Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 23:38, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 02:10.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.

Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.

The Dutchman has helped the Merseyside club win numerous pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-19 Champions League.

However, it is unclear how much longer he will play a part in Liverpool's quest for trophies, with his current contract set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk recently commented on his situation while on international duty, insisting that he is "not in any panic" over his Anfield future.

The centre-back has reiterated his relaxed outlook in an interview with Sky Sports, in which he conceded he has "no idea" whether he will sign a fresh Liverpool deal.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk noted.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone states that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game.

"Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a massive part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

"If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.".

At the age of 35, Van Dijk remains an integral part of the Liverpool squad, demonstrated by the fact he has played every minute of the club's 10 Premier League matches this term.

Van Dijk is now preparing to make his 350th Premier League appearance in Sunday's highly anticipated clash against rivals Manchester United.

The Netherlands international has made 282 of his 349 top-flight appearances in a Liverpool shirt after featuring in 67 Premier League matches for Southampton.

Van Dijk will hope to mark his milestone outing with a victory, although he has had to settle for seven wins in his previous 18 Premier League matches against Man United (D5, L6).

#106318. Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands
